articles.title: Metal-Organic Frameworks Preserved with Ionic Liquids
articles.summary: Researchers have developed a method to reduce damage when manipulating MOFs for electronic devices by filling their pores with an ionic liquid.
articles.content: Researchers have been working on developing metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) for various applications, including gas storage and pollutant capture. MOFs are a class of porous materials that consist of metal ions linked by organic molecules, forming structures with cavities. The unique properties of MOFs arise from their porous nature, which is difficult to achieve with conventional materials. As a result, MOFs have shown great promise for use in functional devices such as chemical sensors and electronic components. Despite their potential, the fragile structure of MOFs can be easily damaged during dry etching, a process that involves using high-energy particles to remove material and create patterns on the surface. The challenge lies in preserving the delicate structures of MOFs while still being able to manipulate them into specific shapes and forms for practical applications. Researchers have developed a method to reduce damage when manipulating metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) for electronic devices. To achieve this, they filled MOF pores with an ionic liquid that increases the material's hardness and preserves its structure during etching. The study, led by Assistant Professor Yumeng Zheng and Professor Kentaro Kinoshita from Tokyo University of Science, built on earlier work demonstrating the strengthening effect of ionic liquids on MOFs. By exploring this approach further, the researchers aimed to enable precise microfabrication of these delicate materials. In their experiment, the researchers used four imidazolium-based ionic liquids that occupied 50%–60% of the pore volume in a copper-based MOF called Cu₃BTC₂. The ionic liquid-filled material was then etched with a focused gallium ion beam at room temperature. The use of ionic liquids greatly improved the mechanical stability of the MOFs, reducing damage from electron and ion beams during etching. This development has significant potential for the creation of precise patterns in MOFs at the nanoscale. The researchers discovered that using an ionic liquid in conjunction with ion beam etching resulted in significantly less damage to the metal-organic framework's (MOF) crystal structure compared to untreated samples. This was attributed to the ionic liquid's ability to absorb heat and dissipate electrical charge during the etching process, thereby protecting the delicate MOF structure. The thermal properties of the ionic liquid may also help buffer temperature changes, while its redistribution of ions can screen local electric fields. Thermal analysis revealed that the treated MOFs had higher decomposition temperatures than their untreated counterparts, indicating improved thermal stability. Hardness tests further showed that all four ionic liquid-treated samples were harder than the untreated material, with stiffness remaining largely unchanged in the process. The use of an ionic liquid during ion beam etching has opened up new possibilities for patterning MOFs at room temperature without requiring specialized equipment such as cryogenic cooling systems. This approach could be extended to other types of MOFs, potentially making them easier to incorporate into practical devices. The successful creation of various patterns using this method is a significant step forward in the development of precise MOF structures. These include intricate designs like a square measuring 5 × 5 µm² and even a Chinese character with etched lines as narrow as 130–300 nm, demonstrating the potential for high-resolution patterning at the nanoscale. Researchers are optimistic about the potential of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) to be used in various electronic devices, including high-sensitivity sensors, separation and analysis devices, and catalytic devices. The method developed for shaping MOFs into precise structures could unlock new applications for these materials, which have been limited by their difficulty to shape. With over 100,000 known MOFs today, this technique has the potential to greatly expand their use in practical devices. This breakthrough is expected to bridge the gap between MOFs' exceptional material properties and their usability in real-world applications. As a result, MOFs could become a foundational technology for various industries. Phys.org : https://phys.org/news/2026-11-metalorganic-frameworks-easier-electronic-devices.html

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Discloses Affair in Memo to Employees
articles.summary: Tech executives, including Nvidia's Jensen Huang, have found themselves at the center of high-profile relationship scandals in recent years.
articles.content: Tech executives have found themselves at the center of high-profile relationship scandals in recent years, with varying degrees of success in managing the fallout. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has become the latest addition to this list after disclosing an affair in a memo to his employees. The company's board is now investigating the matter, raising questions about Huang's future as CEO. Huang joins a long line of tech executives who have faced public scrutiny over their personal relationships. This includes Bill Gates, whose own relationship scandals have been well-documented over the years. The Nvidia CEO's decision to disclose his affair has sparked a mix of reactions within the tech industry, with some questioning whether he will be able to maintain his position as CEO in light of this revelation. The affair between Bezos and Lauren Sánchez was not his first high-profile relationship scandal. The Amazon founder's marriage to MacKenzie Scott was still intact when he sent intimate messages to Sánchez, according to a report. Bezos chose a confrontational approach in handling the situation, taking to Medium with a lengthy post that accused the parent company of extortion and blackmail. He published emails in which the company made it clear they would release compromising photos unless Bezos cooperated. The emails revealed a calculating effort by the company to extract concessions from Bezos. The Amazon founder had to decide whether to give in to their demands or risk the fallout of the scandal being made public. The affair and its aftermath led to a broader discussion about privacy, tabloid media, and the implications for high-profile individuals like Bezos. His split with Scott was also scrutinized in the wake of the scandal. Bezos eventually moved on, marrying Sánchez in 2025 after filing for divorce from Scott in 2019. The couple's decision to end their marriage was described as a "long period of loving exploration and trial separation." The timeline of events surrounding a high-profile scandal at software and data management company Astronomer is equally noteworthy. In July 2025, a video surfaced of Andy Byron, the CEO at the time, embracing Kristin Cabot, the company's chief people officer, during a Coldplay concert. Their affectionate moment was captured on camera by the venue's "kiss cam" and subsequently projected onto big screens for all to see. The incident went viral on TikTok, generating several days' worth of headlines and attention from the public. Astronomer found itself in the midst of a sudden and intense media storm as a result of Byron and Cabot's unexpected display of affection. The sudden departure of Astronomer's CEO following a public display of affection sparked an internal investigation by the company's board into their relationship. This move was likely prompted by the intense media scrutiny that had erupted around the situation. In contrast to Astronomer's more complicated handling of its CEO scandal, Intel took swift action in 2018 when it investigated and subsequently ousted its then-CEO Brian Krzanich over a consensual but prohibited romantic relationship with another employee. This move aligns with Intel's existing non-fraternization policy that prohibits managers from engaging in such relationships. As part of the fallout from Krzanich's departure, Bob Swan, who was serving as CFO at the time, stepped in to lead the company on an interim basis until a new CEO could be appointed. The incident highlights how companies can respond decisively when faced with relationship scandals involving senior executives. Astronomer's tumultuous situation now seems somewhat isolated compared to the more decisive handling of Intel's similar scandal, but it remains to be seen what long-term impact this will have on the company's reputation and future operations. articles.title: House Republicans Choose New Leadership Teams Amid Election Defeat
articles.summary: Representative Steve Scalise has announced he will not contest the minority leader position, stepping down from his current role instead.
articles.content: Washington is abuzz as House and Senate Republicans prepare to choose their leadership teams following a resounding election defeat that swept them from power. In a move seen as a response to party demands for new blood, Representative Steve Scalise has announced he will not contest the minority leader position, stepping down from his current role instead. This decision has triggered a two-way contest in the House, pitting Rep. Scalise against fellow Louisiana Republican and Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan. The stakes are high as both men have strong ties to President Donald Trump and were previously unsuccessful candidates for Speaker of the House after Kevin McCarthy's ouster in 2023. The elections will be held behind closed doors and by secret ballot, with a vote expected later today. The outcome is far from certain, as either Scalise or Jordan needs a majority of their party conference to secure the position. The House Republican leadership election is heating up as Steve Scalise faces a challenge from August Pfluger, the chairman of the Republican Study Committee. Pfluger's bid to become whip, the party's top vote counter and second-in-command in the minority, has sent shockwaves through the party ranks. A House GOP lawmaker supporting Jordan over Scalise emphasized that the party needs to move forward after its election drubbing. "We're ready to move on," they said. "Everything is on the table" as the party seeks to regroup and reassess its agenda in light of the Democratic landslide. Meanwhile, Senate Republicans are also set to hold a closed-door vote to pick their leaders. Majority Leader John Thune of South Dakota appears to have an easy path to minority leader, with no announced opponents at this point. However, some senators have called for delaying the elections to allow time for reflection on the party's poor election performance. A small group of Senate Republicans has expressed concerns that the party needs more time to process its losses and discuss how to move forward. Sen. said that a week ago's election results were "the worst in decades and that the party must have a discussion about what went wrong and how to fix it. The leadership elections in Congress have been put on hold as some Republican senators believe it's essential to discuss the lessons of the midterms before making any decisions. Senate Republicans are seeking a more thorough evaluation of their candidates' plans for leadership before proceeding with the elections scheduled for Tuesday morning. A group of five senators, led by Budget Committee Chairman Ron Johnson of Wisconsin, have sent a letter to Senate Republican Conference Chairman Tom Cotton of Arkansas requesting a robust discussion on how the leadership hopefuls intend to guide the party forward. The letters and statements suggest that some Republicans are hesitant to rush into leadership elections without fully understanding the implications of their choices. This is particularly evident in the case of Senator Johnson, who believes it's crucial to digest and debate the lessons of the midterms before moving forward with the leadership elections. Apart from Tom Cotton, Senate Majority Whip John Barrasso of Wyoming is also expected to retain his position as the second-ranked Republican in the next Congress. As Senate Republicans prepare to select their leadership team, a growing chorus of discontent is emerging among rank-and-file members who are unhappy with the current lineup. Despite this grumbling, no one has yet come forward to challenge Senator Schumer for majority leader. However, Senator Van Hollen has left open the possibility of running for the position amid calls from grassroots supporters looking for an alternative to Schumer. According to a person familiar with his thinking, Van Hollen is now in active listening mode" following an outpouring of support from Democrats who want him to consider taking on the role. In private conversations at the Senate's new-member orientation, incoming lawmakers such as Peggy Flanagan have expressed their excitement about meeting colleagues and beginning work. However, the question of leadership has not yet been discussed among Democrats. Despite having a significant number of votes, Democrats have yet to discuss their leadership positions. Jeffries' large majority in the House means he can afford around 40 defections without jeopardizing his chances of becoming speaker on January 3rd. With no opposition so far, Jeffries and his top lieutenants - Katherine Clark, Pete Aguilar, and Ted Lieu - are set to secure the top four leadership posts: speaker, majority leader, majority whip, and Democratic Caucus chair. articles.title: Experimental Plane Dubbed X-70 Fractal Under Development at NASA
articles.summary: NASA's new experimental plane, the X-70 Fractal, will operate within Earth's atmosphere and has impressive speed capabilities.
articles.content: NASA has been working on a new experimental plane, dubbed the X-70 Fractal, but details about the project have been scarce until now. The X-70 is not designed for space travel and will operate entirely within Earth's atmosphere. It's a subsonic aircraft that can fly much higher than commercial jets, reaching altitudes of over 45,000 feet into the stratosphere. The plane has impressive speed capabilities, with a top speed of around 575 miles per hour, allowing it to cover nearly 1,700 miles in a single flight. This means it can travel vast distances without needing to refuel or make intermediate stops. NASA expects the X-70 Fractal to enable research into complex maneuvers that have never been demonstrated before in crewed aircraft, although specific details about these experiments are still unclear. articles.title: China Introduces Visa-Free Transit Policy for Select Travelers
articles.summary: The new policy allows certain travelers to enter China without a visa for up to 10 days.
articles.content: A recent policy has made it possible for certain travelers to enter China without going through the usual multi-week visa application process. This new rule allows visitors to transit between countries and stay in China for up to 10 days without a visa, as long as their total time in the country does not exceed 240 hours. To take advantage of China's visa-free transit policy, travelers must follow specific guidelines. The key is to enter China from one country and exit through another, distinct nation. For instance, flying from the US to China and then to Japan would be permissible under this policy. Conversely, a trip from the US to China and back to the US would not qualify. The countries eligible for this transit policy include 57 nations, including the United States. A complete list of participating countries can be accessed online. It's essential to note that only passport holders from these designated countries are allowed to participate in visa-free transits within China. Travelers must also adhere to specific entry and exit requirements. The Chinese government has designated certain ports for this policy, and travelers must enter and exit through one of these eligible cities. A comprehensive list of permitted cities is available online, which includes popular destinations like Beijing, Shanghai, and Chengdu. To make the most of this transit policy, travelers can choose to enter and leave China through the same qualifying city or opt for different eligible cities. This flexibility allows visitors to create a customized itinerary that suits their preferences. For example, they could arrive in Shanghai, spend a few days exploring the city, then take a high-speed train to Beijing before departing from another designated port. When testing this policy firsthand, it was essential to stay within the allowed time frame of 240 hours. Travelers must also be mindful of the maximum duration of their stay in China, which is capped at 10 days for visa-free transits. This means that visitors have a limited window to explore the country before departing. By carefully planning their itinerary and adhering to the policy's guidelines, travelers can successfully navigate China without obtaining a traditional visa. However, if they wish to travel beyond the designated areas or stay in China for longer periods, they will need to apply for a Chinese visa. As an American citizen, I was eligible for China's 240-hour visa-free transit policy due to my US passport. To qualify for this policy, travelers must ensure that their routing meets specific requirements. In my case, I departed from Paris on a direct flight to Shanghai and then flew onward to Manila. Since my final destination was the Philippines, my visit to China counted as a long layover rather than an entry into the country. Before making travel arrangements, it's essential to verify that all aspects of your itinerary meet the criteria for the 240-hour visa-free transit policy. This includes checking your passport and the entry and departure ports in China. The Chinese government provides a list of qualifying passports and entry-exit ports on their official website, which travelers should consult before booking flights or accommodations. Travelers should also consider organizing their documentation to prove they intend to stay no more than 10 days in China. As I approached the check-in counter at Air France, the agent asked me for my Chinese visa, which I didn't have in hand. Panicked, I quickly searched online for a solution and presented the results to him, but he was unimpressed. The agent switched to English and informed me that the information I had found was not official. I pleaded with him to let me speak to someone who could clarify the situation, and after a moment of hesitation, he phoned a colleague. A Chinese-speaking Air France representative joined our conversation and explained that my research was correct - there is indeed a new policy for 10-day visa-free transit in China. However, this agent also emphasized that I needed to provide proof of onward travel to avoid any issues. I rummaged through my phone and found the screenshot of my ticket to the Philippines, which I had saved earlier. The Air France representative was satisfied with this documentation and assured me that it would suffice for transit purposes. As a traveler in such situations, it's crucial to be prepared and have all necessary documents printed out or easily accessible on your phone. This includes your flight itinerary, accommodation information, and official visa-free transit policy details. Upon arrival in China, international travelers are required to complete a digital arrival form, regardless of whether they hold a visa or not. The form asks about the presence of a Chinese visa and offers an option for those using the 240-hour visa-free transit policy. The completed form generates a QR code that serves as proof of compliance with immigration regulations. Travelers should screenshot this code and be prepared to present it, along with their onward ticket, when required by immigration officials during processing. Upon presenting my ticket to Manila, immigration officials didn't ask for the QR code I had obtained earlier but did request to see it as part of their processing. After reviewing everything, they stamped my passport with a transit visa, which included my date of entry into China and the expected departure date. With this done, I was cleared to proceed and made my way through customs, feeling relieved that the process had gone smoothly. According to Zhang, working with a reputable travel company can simplify the arrival experience even further by providing VIP airport pickups for those using the 10-day transit visa. This service would have an airport concierge meet travelers at the gate and guide them through the visa application step-by-step, alleviating some of the stress associated with navigating unfamiliar procedures. One thing that stood out to me during my visit was the stark difference in technology usage compared to what I'm used to back home. The absence of popular apps like Uber and Google Maps initially presented a challenge, but local hotels such as PuLi Shanghai and Upper House Shanghai provided valuable assistance in getting set up with alternative solutions. Their teams helped me download essential Chinese apps that would prove indispensable during my stay. China has become increasingly reliant on digital communication, and visitors will find that WeChat is an essential tool for staying connected during their stay. This popular app is used by everyone in China, including the guest experiences team at Capella Shanghai, Jian Ye Li, who provided me with cultural tours of the hotel's neighborhood. To access vital apps like Google Workplace and Instagram, it's crucial to have a compatible internet connection while in mainland China. If your existing carrier offers roaming services in China, you may be able to receive verification texts and stay connected online. Alternatively, consider purchasing a travel eSIM that explicitly covers China. I used Airalo, a travel eSIM, and my French home carrier Free to connect to the internet during my visit, allowing me to access essential apps without any issues. Zhang recommends installing a VPN on your laptop or tablet if you need to stay connected to services like Google, WhatsApp, or Instagram while using public Wi-Fi. To ensure seamless connectivity, it's also recommended that you arrange for a paid VPN subscription before leaving for China. I personally used Astrill VPN to access Gmail and YouTube on my laptop, and this worked perfectly throughout my stay. articles.title: New species of insect found living on spider's web in China
articles.summary: A newly discovered species of insect has been found to live its entire life cycle on a spider's web, raising questions about the delicate balance between these tiny creatures and their massive arachnid hosts.
articles.content: A newly discovered species of insect has been found to live its entire life cycle on a spider's web, raising questions about the delicate balance between these tiny creatures and their massive arachnid hosts. The insect, known as Heissophila sinica, is a type of true bug that feeds on other small insects. It is able to navigate the intricate silk threads of the spider's web with ease, often going unnoticed by its host. This unique relationship has left scientists fascinated about how these tiny creatures coexist with their larger counterparts. Researchers at China Agricultural University in Beijing have been studying web-loving bugs in China since the 2020s. According to lead researcher Haoyang Xiong, these insects are rare and occur in low numbers, making them difficult to study. They also exhibit unusual behavior, which has sparked interest among scientists. The study of web-loving bugs is still in its early stages, with many species remaining poorly understood. Heissophila sinica is no exception, having been found in just one location so far - a region in China's Fujian province where funnel web spiders are common. The discovery of Heissophila sinica has shed new light on a unique relationship between insects and arachnids. The tiny reddish bugs have been found to thrive in a region of China's Fujian province where funnel web spiders are common. Their physical characteristics set them apart from other known species, leading researchers to conclude that they belong to an entirely new genus. A key factor contributing to their survival is the size difference between the spider and the insects themselves, which may deter the spider from seeing them as prey. The bugs feed on scraps left behind by the spiders after meals, as well as web-dwelling mites - some of which are even parasites of the spiders. They also gather around the spider's molting sites to drink its body fluids, a behavior that has left scientists unsure about the nature of their relationship with the arachnids. Researchers note that Heissophila sinica may be commensal organisms, neither helping nor hindering the spiders' survival. This phenomenon highlights the complexity and diversity of interactions between different species in their natural habitats. The discovery of a newly described insect has shed light on its unique lifestyle, where it may spend its entire life on a spider's web. The team has observed all stages of this insect's development, from eggs to juveniles and adults, coexisting on the same web. Despite its sticky surroundings, the insect is able to move around on the silk without getting stuck. Researchers believe that the insect's unusual feet may be responsible for this ability, as they lack many of the complex structures found in other insects' feet. This adaptation allows the insect to thrive in an environment where most others would struggle. The research team has been commended for their fieldwork efforts and documentation of the natural history of these bizarre insects. Randall Schuh from the American Museum of Natural History in New York praises the team's dedication, noting that studying such tiny creatures can be challenging due to the harsh conditions they inhabit. To further understand the evolution of these web-dwelling insects, the research team plans to expand their collection efforts in China and surrounding regions. By gathering genetic data, they aim to shed more light on the mysterious lives of these spider web tenants, providing valuable insights into the complex interactions between species in their natural habitats. articles.title: Breakthroughs in Neutrino Research Recognized by Nobel Prize Committee
articles.summary: The recent Nobel prize announcement recognizes Francis Halzen's leadership on the IceCube Neutrino Observatory in Antarctica.
articles.content: Breakthroughs in neutrino research have long been awaited by scientists, and a recent Nobel prize announcement is being seen as a major milestone in this field. The winner of this year's award was Francis Halzen, recognized for his leadership on the IceCube Neutrino Observatory in Antarctica. This research facility has made significant contributions to our understanding of neutrinos, which are subatomic particles that have unique properties. They come in three distinct flavours and can oscillate between these identities as they travel through space. Neutrinos' ability to change identities is a key aspect of their behaviour. This property is linked to the mass of these particles, but despite extensive research, scientists still do not fully comprehend how neutrinos acquire their mass. The study of neutrinos has far-reaching implications for our understanding of the universe. Neutrinos produced in stars, including our own sun, are created as a by-product of nuclear fusion processes that also generate light. These same phenomena play a role in stellar deaths, such as supernovae, which are massive explosions that occur when a star runs out of fuel. One notable example is Supernova 1987A, the closest supernova to our solar system in centuries, observed across various parts of the electromagnetic spectrum. This event was particularly interesting because it marked the first time scientists were able to connect observed neutrinos with such an explosion. Hours before light from the supernova became visible, three different neutrino detectors on Earth detected an influx of these elusive particles. The discovery of neutrinos arriving before light provided valuable insights into this cosmic event. It also highlighted the unique properties of neutrinos that allow them to travel long distances through space without interacting with matter. The detection of neutrinos from Supernova 1987A underscores their role as messengers from distant stellar events, providing scientists with a new perspective on these phenomena. Neutrinos have long been known for their ability to pass through matter with ease, barely interacting with other particles as they stream through space. This characteristic has proven invaluable in helping scientists study distant stellar events, including supernovae like 1987A. By observing the neutrinos emitted by such explosions, researchers can gain a deeper understanding of these cataclysmic occurrences and their impact on the surrounding environment. The IceCube Neutrino Observatory at the South Pole in Antarctica has been instrumental in harnessing the power of neutrinos for astrophysical research. This cutting-edge facility was conceptualized by a team led by Halzen, who envisioned using neutrinos as a lens to peer into the cosmos and uncover new insights about the universe. The creation of IceCube marked the beginning of a new era in neutrino astrophysics, with thousands of scientists collaborating over the years to develop and refine this groundbreaking technology. The images captured by IceCube's neutrino detector reveal a complex and asymmetric landscape, filled with mysterious blobs that are ripe for investigation. This asymmetry has piqued the interest of researchers, who often rely on symmetry to indicate the presence of interesting phenomena - but in this case, the unknown is all the more intriguing. Neilson now leads a research group focused on deciphering the secrets of the galactic centre through neutrino observations, specifically seeking to understand what accelerates particles to relativistic speeds within that region. The challenge lies in correlating neutrino sources with high-energy light sources, which are believed to originate from the same location.
